turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling nervous and devoted, assured his mother that he would always follow her teachings and respect his father and grandfather as she wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was relieved to hear her son's promise, and urged him to stay true to his word, her eyes filled with a mixture of hope and sorrow.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid, attentive to O-lan’s comfort, quietly approached the eldest son and his new wife, urging them to continue supporting their mother with the same care and devotion.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung, seeing the worry in his wife's eyes, reassured her that he would take care of everything as she had taught him to. He promised to make sure their eldest son followed through with her wishes, keeping her guidance close to heart.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan, feeling a sense of relief and yet a deep worry, urged Wang Lung to ensure that the eldest son and the maid worked together to support the family.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung, seeing the concern in O-lan’s eyes, promised to make sure the eldest son married as she wished, and that the maid would be there to support them all.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, hesitant but respectful, nodded to his mother and father, promising to do as she wished, his heart heavy with worry but determined to bring her peace.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan, feeling a mix of relief and urgency, told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she needed to see the arrangements for the marriage finalised soon, her heart heavy with the knowledge that time was running out.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, his voice soft and hesitant, assured O-lan that he would do everything in his power to make her wishes come true, his heart heavy with the responsibility.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan, feeling the weight of her illness and the urgency of her wish, told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she needed to see the marriage preparations move forward quickly, her heart aching for the future of her family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice barely above a whisper, promising O-lan that he would hasten the marriage preparations as much as possible, his heart aching for her.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan, feeling the urgency of her wish, told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she needed to see the preparations move faster, her heart heavy with the knowledge that time was slipping away.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung, his eyes filled with a mixture of worry and determination, reassured O-lan that he would make sure everything was in place as soon as possible, his heart set on fulfilling her wishes.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice barely above a whisper, promising O-lan that he would do all he could to speed up the marriage preparations, his heart heavy with the knowledge that each passing moment brought him closer to losing her.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid stepped forward, her eyes downcast, and quietly assured O-lan that she would ensure the household ran smoothly while the eldest son prepared for the marriage.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan pressed her husband and son, her voice tinged with urgency, telling them that haste was crucial as she felt her strength waning each day.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice trembling, reassuring O-lan that he would do everything in his power to make sure the preparations were completed as quickly as possible.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan that he would personally see to the arrangements, his voice steady and determined, though his heart was heavy with anxiety.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan pressed her husband and son, her voice tinged with urgency, telling them that haste was crucial as she felt her strength waning each day.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He nodded again, his voice barely above a whisper, telling O-lan that he understood the urgency and would do his best to arrange everything quickly.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
